subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should configured model refs be catalog-checked as advisory warnings by default, or should invalid catalog misses become strict config errors?
rationale: Current code intentionally supports dynamic provider model IDs, so automation should not choose fail-open versus fail-closed semantics without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Advisory validation by default
options.body: Warn in config validate and doctor when trusted catalog evidence says a configured ref is unknown, while keeping dynamic or unverified refs usable.

options.title: Strict catalog errors
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs during config writes/validation, accepting the compatibility risk for custom and forward-compatible provider models.

options.title: Fold into broader model reconcile work
options.body: Keep this as part of the broader model-configuration reconcile discussion before landing a narrower validation change.

recommendation.title: Advisory validation by default
recommendation.body: Warn in config validate and doctor when trusted catalog evidence says a configured ref is unknown, while keeping dynamic or unverified refs usable.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent history across model failover, provider identity, and the documented user-visible fallback behavior that shapes this product tradeoff.
